images.title: Celsius and Fahrenheit side by side
images.purpose: Shows that 0 °C sits at 32 °F and 25 °C at 77 °F, so Fahrenheit is 9/5 times Celsius plus 32, not a simple ratio.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two tall vertical thermometer scales side by side with a horizontal arrow between them.
images.exact_structure: Two vertical scales of equal height standing side by side. Left scale in teal (#0072B2), titled °C at the top, with exactly two labelled ticks: 0 low down and 25 higher up. Right scale in amber (#E69F00), titled °F at the top, with exactly two labelled ticks: 32 level with the 0 on the left scale and 77 level with the 25. One thin dark dotted line joins 0 to 32. One reddish purple (#CC79A7) arrow joins 25 to 77, labelled above it × 9/5 + 32. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: 0 °C is 32 °F, so converting multiplies by 9/5 and then adds 32; it is not a simple ratio.
images.description: Shows that 0 °C sits at 32 °F and 25 °C at 77 °F, so Fahrenheit is 9/5 times Celsius plus 32, not a simple ratio.

image_decisions.why: Aligned scales show that zero does not match zero, which is why the conversion is not proportional.
